references.extraction: Transcribed printed numerical labels after rendering page; no values estimated from bar heights.
references.definition: Percentage of Australian adults aged 18+ who went recreational fishing at least once in the preceding 12 months. Weighted Regional Wellbeing Survey estimates.
notes: 2018 and 2020 are survey reference years, not 2023 publication year.
The 2020 estimate is 20.0%, with a reported 95% confidence range 19.2–20.9%.
2018 headline 21.4% is rounded; Table 4.2 separately reports 21.37%.

references.extraction: Transcribed exact one-decimal numeric labels after rendering.
references.definition: Percentage of adults aged 18+ in each residence jurisdiction who fished in preceding 12 months.
notes: NSW and ACT are one combined survey group. Do not split their rate or counts.
Rates for 2018 are one-decimal labels in Figure 4.4; Table 4.2 contains two-decimal 2018 rates.
Report states no statistically significant change within any state or territory from 2018 to 2020; avoid claiming that every numerical change is a proven trend.
2020 is the latest comparable national wave in this report; later state surveys have different scopes.

references.definition: Estimated adults who fished at least once in 2018, scaled using revised June 2019 adult population estimates. Fisher counts rounded to nearest 100.
notes: Counts are 2018 estimates, not 2020 counts.
Children under 18 are excluded.

National 4,218,600 includes 1,900 people in other/no-fixed-address categories. Sum of displayed jurisdiction counts plus other differs by 100 from national total due rounding; do not force reconciliation.

references.figure: Figure 4.2 as printed; referred to as Figure 4.8 in surrounding prose
references.extraction: Transcribed printed numeric labels after rendering; 2018 values also confirmed in prose on printed p 43.
references.definition: Percentage within each adult age or gender category who fished in the preceding 12 months.
notes: Gender categories are reproduced as reported; no claim that survey categories describe all identities.
The 30–44 age group fell from 26.6% to 20.6%. Report describes 18–29 increase and 45–64 decrease as not statistically significant.
Observed differences do not establish that COVID-19 caused the changes.

references.figure: Figure 4.1 as printed; referred to as Figure 4.7 in surrounding prose
references.extraction: Transcribed printed numeric labels after rendering.
references.definition: Estimated share of adults undertaking each activity once or more in a typical 2–3-year period, based on 2018 survey.
notes: This is NOT annual participation.
The report reinterprets answers as a typical 2–3-year period after participant follow-up; see printed p 42 footnote 7.
Multiple activities can be selected, so percentages must not be added.
Use chart subtitle to distinguish fishing 30.8% here from annual 20.0% in 2020.

references.extraction: Transcribed table matrix after text extraction and visual verification; summed urban and regional origin/destination cells into state pairs; retained only interstate pairs.
references.definition: Estimated full-time-equivalent employment supported across all industries by recreational-fishing-related expenditure of residents of origin regions, occurring in destination economies. Includes direct and flow-on effects in 2018–19.
notes: Arrows must be labelled economic contributions, NOT people moving, fishing trips, catches, or direct spending.
Includes interregional business supply-chain and household spending effects.
Includes ACT as a separate economic region even though participation combines NSW/ACT.
Within-state flows are excluded.
Source Sydney→Sydney cell literally reads 9 Ti 649, so it is stored as null in the transcription. It does not enter any interstate aggregate. No value was inferred.
Published matrix values are rounded to whole FTE; aggregated totals inherit rounding.
A map can use an origin-state selector to avoid overlapping bilateral lines.

references.definition: Modelled economic contribution by expenditure category, 2018–19. GDP figures are AUD millions; employment is full-time-equivalent jobs.
notes: GDP contribution is not the amount fishers spent.
Flow-on comprises production- and consumption-induced effects.
Figures are source-rounded: direct plus flow-on can differ from reported total by 1 million. Preserve reported totals.
These are historical 2018–19 dollars, not inflation-adjusted current dollars.

employment_matrix_transcription.missing_cell: Sydney to Sydney is corrupt in the source; null retained and only interstate aggregations used.
